result.reason: This is the core job, and a dedicated, cheap product already does it. tfgraport.pl generates the monthly UFG contract register, including the July 2026 file due 14 Aug, and sends it as CSV/JSON or through the API. UFG's FAQ settles the open question on payments: actual advance payments and refunds, with dates, are part of the register. That raises the effort somewhat, but the existing tools already handle it. The duty is not new either; the register has been mandatory since 2018. Booking systems such as Otiumo cover the space next to it and may add exports. A solo founder would be entering a market that is already served, so differentiation is thin. Merlinx's export capability was not checked.

result.competitor: I found no dedicated software, generator or SaaS. A gov.pl Wody Polskie page titled 'Legalizacja urządzenia wodnego' turned up in search, but my fetch only returned the generic gov.pl portal page. Whether there is an ePUAP form or e-submission was not verified. The existing alternatives are licensed hydrogeologists and operat writers, drilling firms (for example the dambat.pl blog guide) and advisory blogs (ongeo.pl, which sells plot reports, not legalisation). An expired pepper.pl post advertised 'darmowe zalegalizowanie studni' but did not say who offered it. Wody Polskie's own guidance and the local nadzór wodny are free alternatives for the paperwork. The professional documentation step is the real cost, and software cannot replace it.
result.duty: Art. 524a Prawo wodne, added by the Ustawa z 19.06.2026 o zmianie ustawy Prawo wodne (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1033), which the President signed. It took effect on 17 or 18 Aug 2026 (sources differ), and I could not read the official PDF to settle the date. Owners of groundwater intakes built without a water permit or notification before the act took effect are exempt from the legalisation fee (about PLN 6,600) and from the art. 472aa administrative penalty (500% of the variable abstraction fee, min PLN 5,000, max PLN 1M) if they file a complete legalisation application with Wody Polskie water supervision (nadzór wodny) by 31 Dec 2027. Earlier drafts said 30 Sep 2027. Each water installation needs its own application. Exemption from the permit applies below 5 m3/day (annual average); 30 m depth is the reported threshold. It is a one-off duty, not recurring. Media report a case in which a farmer was fined PLN 60k.
result.market: There is no official count. Press estimates (from coverage of the bill) say up to about 40,000 farms could benefit, plus non-farm owners. Other press speaks of 'thousands' of owners and 'hundreds of thousands' unaware of the rules. Wody Polskie reportedly imposed about PLN 14M in fines for illegal groundwater abstraction over two years. I found no register-based figure.
result.reason: The duty is real. The 19 Jun 2026 amendment (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1033) adds art. 524a Prawo wodne, which waives the roughly PLN 6,600 legalisation fee and the PLN 5,000 to 1M fines if a complete application reaches a Wody Polskie water-supervision unit by 31 Dec 2027. Sources disagree on the entry-into-force date (17 or 18 Aug 2026). I found no SaaS, document generator or free state tool, but the core job is an operat wodnoprawny or hydrogeological documentation, which needs a licensed professional. Software adds little. It is a one-off with no recurrence, and the only market figure is about 40k farms (a press estimate). Buyers are scattered rural owners, best reached through drillers. The revive is justified as a deadline-driven one-off, but the score stays low.

result.competitor: AutoSoft (iautosoft.pl/cepik.html), a "Program dla Stacji Demontażu Pojazdów", claims full two-way CEPiK 2.0 integration for SDP with real-time data exchange. It handles the certificate set-up: you generate the CSR in the program, apply through the OWoC service and load the .p12 file. Its pricing is not public. The ministry FAQ says ready-made products are on the market and that integration is the producer's job. A software vendor had to be in place by the 30 Jun 2026 deadline, and the workshops told stations to apply for production certificates by 15 Jun 2026. So the forced-purchase wave has already passed and stations are now locked into vendors. I did not find a public list of vendors, so the number of other integrated producers is unverified.
result.duty: Confirmed and in force in Poland. The Minister of Digital Affairs notice of 28 Aug 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1227) set 30 Jun 2026 as the go-live date for dismantling stations (SDP) and collection points (PZP) to send dismantling and incomplete-vehicle data to CEP. The official CEPiK FAQ (gov.pl) confirms the production environment has been available since 30.06.2026. Stations must send each certificate (ioDP) "niezwłocznie" (without delay), or within 3 working days if a failure outside their control prevents it. CEPiK offers only an API, with no state app and no web form. Each user needs their own SSL certificate on a crypto card, and each site needs a VPN certificate; both are valid for 2 years. Stations must buy software from the market. The FAQ also says the law sets no penalty for late transmission. The certificate templates and a separate register for each certificate type are set by Dz.U. 2026 poz. 857 (claimed; I saw it only in search results). BDO vehicle cards continue.
result.market: I found no current register count. The latest figure I found, FORS data cited in search results, is about 924 stations and 134 collection points at the end of 2014, so roughly 1,000 to 1,100 businesses. The current figure would be in the voivodeship marshals' lists (wykazy marszałków), which I did not reach. About 585,562 cars were dismantled in 2025, according to CEPiK data reported by Interia.
result.reason: The duty is real and recurring: every dismantling certificate has to go to CEPiK by API, and that can only be done through third-party software. But the buying trigger (30 Jun 2026) has already passed. Stations had to have integrated software and certificates by mid-June 2026, and at least one dedicated SDP vendor (AutoSoft) openly claims CEPiK 2.0 integration. The market is small, at roughly 1,000 businesses, and the law sets no penalty for late transmission. Building it means getting test-environment access, handling crypto cards and VPN, and keeping up with API changes, which is not a simple MVP. A late entrant could only win switchers from weak incumbents. That leaves a small niche with an incumbent already in place, so this is refuted as an open gap.

result.competitor: No Polish commercial product found that advertises generating or exporting the wykaz umów to UFG. Searches covering Merlinx, booking systems, a 'TFG module' and 'wykaz umów' turned up only generic travel software (PHPTRAVELS, Anolla). Merlinx's export capability is still unknown. The main substitute is the free state option: firms can keep the register directly in the UFG system, and the ZPUTFG platform handles declarations and reports. That covers the core job manually for low-volume agencies. No UFG import format (CSV/XML) or API documentation was found publicly, which is a risk for an MVP.
result.duty: Confirmed (Polish law, in force). Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1806 was published 17 Dec 2025. Its general start date is 1 Jan 2026, and selected provisions apply from 1 Jul 2026. The consolidated text is Dz.U. 2026 poz. 925, with the law as it stood on 1 Jul 2026. Under the new art. 9 ust. 2a, organisers and linked-travel-service facilitators who keep the contract register (wykaz umów) outside the system in art. 7 ust. 1 pkt 3 lit. a must send it through that system by the 14th of each month for the previous calendar month. Under ust. 2b, data already in the system must be updated within 14 days of a change. Under ust. 2c-2d, if a firm defaults, UFG issues a call through the system with a deadline of up to 14 days and notifies the marshal. UFG can then ask the marshal for an administrative decision. Search summaries indicate the register fields now include the contract type and subject, revised price and place fields, and a new pkt 10 on whether advance payments (przedpłaty) are collected. The pre-2026 register already had to list the dates and amounts of advance payments actually received (2016 UFG presentation). That supports the chamber's point that payments are reported, though the exact current wording was not read. The deletion and 3-year ban were not checked in the statute text: the PDFs could not be parsed. They rely on the ministry's interpellation reply cited in the claim. Monthly TFG/TFP contribution declarations already existed.
result.market: About 5,000 tour organisers and linked-travel-service facilitators, per the ITRP letter of 2 Jun 2026, holding ~932 mln PLN in TFG/TFP accounts. This was not checked against the CEOTiPUNPUT register count. The share that keeps the register outside the UFG system, and so faces the monthly transfer, is unknown.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. It comes from art. 9 ust. 2a-2d of the tourist events act as amended by Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1806, which applies from 1 Jul 2026. A firm that keeps its contract register outside the UFG system must send it through that system by the 14th of each month and update changes within 14 days. If it doesn't, UFG issues a call and then asks the marshal for a decision. I found no commercial product that exports this register to UFG. The free UFG system lets firms keep the register directly in it, which is a manual substitute for micro agencies with few contracts. The upload format, an API and Merlinx support remain unverified. The buyer group (~5,000 firms) is reachable through ITRP, but its willingness to pay is uncertain.

result.competitor: No dedicated Polish tool for the municipal registration number was found. Searches for Hotres, Smoobu and IdoBooking found no confirmation that they offer a registration-number field, so this is unverified, but channel managers will very likely add one. Tax and legal firms (iFirma, Captain Legal, MDDP, Podatnik.info) already publish guidance and could offer done-for-you registration. Whether the state builds a free CWTON/ewidencja e-form is not confirmed, but the bill design (gmina-run, numbers issued centrally) makes a free state channel likely.
result.duty: Not yet in force. Druk 2865 (UC135, amending the hotel services act) would require an entry in a gmina-run ewidencja/CWTON and a registration number from the wójt, burmistrz or prezydent miasta, shown in every listing. It would also require house rules, a 24h contact, a visible notice outside the unit and a fire-safety declaration. Fines would be up to 50,000 PLN, and a fee is reportedly charged for the entry and for changes. Status: first reading with autopoprawka 2865-A on 2 Sep 2026. After the second reading in October 2026 the bill went back to committee instead of to a vote. Finwire (6 Oct 2026) forecasts passage in H1 2027. The 1 Jan 2028 ban by wspólnoty/municipalities is planned, with a majority of all eligible voters required. EU Reg. 2024/1028 has applied since 20 May 2026, but Poland has not set up the register or a single digital entry point, so hosts cannot get numbers yet. The existing gmina ewidencja under the current hotel services act is already in force for some objects (Kraków accepts applications electronically, by post or in person). Recurrence for hosts looks low: a one-off registration plus updates. No sources found on recurring host reports; platforms pass nights and guests to gminas.
result.market: About 65,000 flats were offered for short-term rental in 2024, nearly 60,000 of them on Airbnb (estimates from the Polish Short-Term Rental Association, PSWK, cited by Demagog and Finwire). Mieszkanicznik estimates about 60,000. Eurostat counts 44.4m platform nights in Poland in 2025. Many of these are professional operators, not private hosts.
result.reason: The duty is not yet law. Druk 2865 went back to committee after the October 2026 second reading, and passage is forecast for H1 2027, so dates and the final procedure are unknown. For hosts the core job is mostly a one-off registration with a gmina, plus putting the number in listings. Platforms carry the recurring data reporting. A free state register (CWTON) is planned, and channel managers will likely add the number field. The market is about 65,000 units, many run by managers who already use PMS tools. Pain is high once the rule is enforced (fines up to 50k PLN), but recurrence and willingness to pay for software are low. A one-off registration service could work in a short window. Worth watching, not building now.

result.competitor: No Polish tool found that keeps the statutory staff register, ID-card log, criminal-record dates or qualification and exam expiry. Anolla (Polish-language, free plan) does guard scheduling and bookings; it mentions training and certificates in passing but not the statutory register. ShiftFlow does time tracking for guards. Ajax PRO Desktop is an alarm-company platform with staff roles. Generic HR file software (e.g. Asystent Akta Osobowe) has nothing specific to security. result.duty: Real, under the ustawa z 22.08.1997 o ochronie osób i mienia (consolidated text Dz.U. 2025 poz. 532, which exists). Agencies must keep personnel documentation, including the staff register (wykaz pracowników ochrony) with name, birth details, address, PESEL, date of qualified-list entry and the authority that made it, ID card (legitymacja) number, contract start and end dates and criminal-record check dates. They must also keep a log of issued, exchanged and returned ID cards (Dz.U. 2017 poz. 1306/1307), on paper or electronically. Records are kept 5 years after the business closes, and the agency must notify the licensing authority (organ koncesyjny) when it starts, suspends or ends the activity. The 14-day notice in art. 18 ust. 3 covers changes to concession data under ust. 1 pkt 1, 1a, 2 and 4 (owners, managers and the qualified persons among them), not every change of staff. A separate 14-day duty falls on the qualified guard personally, who must report changes to the voivodeship police commander. Medical and psychological exams are every 3 years per a secondary commentary, not checked in the statute. Not verified: the current wording of the documentation article (the lexlege fetch failed), penalties and revocation grounds, and how often criminal-record re-checks are required. Frequency is mostly event-driven (hires, exits, expiries) plus police and ministry inspections.
result.market: No current count found. Wprost (around 2000) put concessions at about 8,000. The ministry tracks concession holders in an e-koncesje system but no public total was found. Oferteo lists 3,331 security firms, which is a directory, not the register. The sector is dominated by large groups (Impel, Solid, Konsal), and the share of tiny agencies is unknown. A rough estimate is a few thousand concession holders; not verified.
result.reason: The duty exists, but it is mostly event-driven record-keeping rather than a recurring filing. Agencies must keep a staff register (wykaz pracowników ochrony) with PESEL, qualified-list entry, ID card number, contract dates and criminal-record check dates. They also keep a log of issued and returned guard ID cards (Dz.U. 2017 poz. 1306/1307) and retain records for 5 years. The claim overstates the 14-day rule (art. 18 ust. 3). It covers changes to concession data, such as owners or managers on the qualified list, not every guard hire. Penalties and the current consolidated text (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 532) were not checked. No Polish tool for the register or expiry tracking was found; Anolla and ShiftFlow only do scheduling. The number of firms is unknown, and pain and willingness to pay look modest.

result.reason: Duty is real: Animal Health Act of 21 Nov 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1795, in force 18 Mar 2026), art. 68 pt 4, requires apiary location and hive count to be sent to the district vet by 31 Mar and 30 Sep. Registration is under Regulation Dz.U. 2026 poz. 292. Only one PLW notice was fetched, and it names no penalties. Submission is a simple form, in person or by e-Doręczenia/Profil Zaufany. The market is large (many tens of thousands of beekeepers) but fragmented. Distribution through beekeeper associations is possible. The idea is a weak standalone product and fits better as a feature of a hive-record app.

The AML duty on brokers (ustawa AML of 1 Mar 2018, art. 2 ust. 1) is real, with fines up to 1 mln PLN (art. 150 ust. 2), per rpms.pl. I could not confirm the 31 Dec 2026 identification-form deadline in a primary source. A second source (dudkowiak.com) describes a draft (UC75) with SIGIIF registration of "other" entities on 29 Oct-11 Nov 2026, so the timeline is unstable. The duty is mostly one-off plus procedures, not recurring. Competition is crowded: procedure packs (Akademia LTCA, RPMS), Comarch apfino for accounting offices, and generic AML tools. The state's own SIGIIF form is free. Willingness to pay is low, so it is a thin niche.

EUDR (Reg. 2023/1115 as amended by 2025/2650, published 23 Dec 2025) is in force. Application dates are 30 Dec 2026 for large and medium firms and 30 Jun 2027 for micro and small firms. One adviser says micro and small timber firms start on 30 Dec 2026. I did not check this against the regulation text. The amendment puts the DDS duty only on the first operator placing goods on the EU market. Downstream traders, who are most small roasters, chocolate makers and furniture sellers, are exempt from filing their own DDS. So the buyer group is mostly not an operator, and the "simplified declaration" for micro operators was not confirmed. Competition: global platforms such as Tracextech already offer EUDR furniture and wood DDS and supplier data collection for Poland, plus Polish consultancies (Akademia LTCA, Crowe, Grant Thornton). I found no Polish register count of small firms. A Polish implementing act is still a draft. Demand is thin and dates keep changing.

Duty is real: the 2015 act on ozone-depleting substances and F-gases (art. 19 CRO, art. 39 reports) requires operators to keep device cards in CRO (run by ICHP; threshold 3 kg or 5 t CO2e). The annual BDS report is due 28 Feb. CRO was updated in March 2024 for Reg. 2024/573. I could not confirm current penalty amounts, current report scope, operator counts, or a commercial competitor. The free state CRO and BDS cover the core filing. No dedicated servicer software was found in 3 searches, but the search was weak. Real pain is on servicers, who often enter data on the client's account. Buyers are fragmented, with low willingness to pay. Niche, so a low score.

The duty is real. Dental X-ray rooms need a permit or notification under Prawo atomowe, and operational tests are set by the 2022 Health Ministry regulation (Dz.U. 2022 poz. 2759, in force from 28 Dec 2022). I could not confirm the current test frequencies or penalties. Older sources give 12 to 24 months for specialist tests, but those are for older or draft rules. I found no Polish software product, and no free state tool, for dental X-ray records. Service firms with medical physicists and radiation protection inspectors probably do the testing, but I found no specific offers. No count of dental X-ray rooms was found; PAA reports over 4,000 units in all sectors. The work is physical measurement done by licensed labs, not software. Test intervals of 1 to 2 years make it infrequent, and the buyer base is fragmented.

The duty is real. Vans of 2.5-3.5 t on international haulage need a G2V2 tachograph from 1 Jul 2026, and Infor and Trans.info report fines up to 12k PLN. I found no postponement. Exemptions exist for own-account use, domestic-only work and vehicles carrying up to 9 persons. The core job is already served. Tachospeed Expert (14-day demo), Webfleet Tacho Manager (download, analysis and archiving, with data kept for at least 2 years), Inelo TachoZdalnie/TachoReader remote download, and the MT TACHO smartphone card reader all do it. Prices were not found. I did not find a register count; the claim's 40k vehicles is unchecked. Only a thin cheap layer for 1-3 vans might remain, with weak differentiation.
